non_builder_commands.name: ASKING
non_builder_commands.rationale: Cluster redirect handling sends ASKING and the redirected command as one connection-local exchange; a standalone builder would make unsafe separation easy.

non_builder_commands.name: CLUSTER COUNT-FAILURE-REPORTS
non_builder_commands.rationale: Node-local cluster administration remains an explicitly routed raw operation.

non_builder_commands.name: CLUSTER MIGRATION
non_builder_commands.rationale: Redis 8 cluster migration administration is not part of automatic client routing and must target a deliberate node.

non_builder_commands.name: CLUSTER MYSHARDID
non_builder_commands.rationale: This node-local topology inspection command requires an explicitly selected cluster node.

non_builder_commands.name: CLUSTER SLOT-STATS
non_builder_commands.rationale: This node-local Redis 8.2 administration command is available through a deliberately routed raw request.

non_builder_commands.name: CLUSTER SYNCSLOTS
non_builder_commands.rationale: Cluster slot synchronization mutates node-local state and is intentionally not exposed as an ordinary routed builder.

non_builder_commands.name: JSON.DEBUG HELP
non_builder_commands.rationale: JSON.DEBUG MEMORY has a typed builder; the module help variant is an operator-facing raw reply and remains raw-only.

non_builder_commands.name: PSUBSCRIBE
non_builder_commands.rationale: Pattern subscription changes a dedicated socket into Pub/Sub mode and is owned by the streaming session API.

non_builder_commands.name: PSYNC
non_builder_commands.rationale: Replication handshakes and replication-stream consumption are outside the request/response client contract.

non_builder_commands.name: PUNSUBSCRIBE
non_builder_commands.rationale: Pattern unsubscription is part of the stateful Pub/Sub session and its acknowledgement stream.

non_builder_commands.name: READONLY
non_builder_commands.rationale: Replica-read connections issue READONLY during connection setup so reconnects restore the state before routing reads.

non_builder_commands.name: READWRITE
non_builder_commands.rationale: The public cluster clients own their read-routing mode; ad hoc connection-state reversal is only available on an explicitly owned raw session.

non_builder_commands.name: SSUBSCRIBE
non_builder_commands.rationale: Sharded Pub/Sub uses a dedicated standalone session or a slot-aware Cluster session that follows the channel slot's owner.

non_builder_commands.name: SUBSCRIBE
non_builder_commands.rationale: Subscription changes the connection protocol mode and is exposed through a dedicated streaming session rather than a stateless command builder.

non_builder_commands.name: SUNSUBSCRIBE
non_builder_commands.rationale: Sharded unsubscription is owned by the dedicated standalone or slot-aware Cluster Pub/Sub session and its confirmation handling.

non_builder_commands.name: SYNC
non_builder_commands.rationale: Legacy replication handshakes and replication-stream consumption are outside the request/response client contract.

non_builder_commands.name: TRIMSLOTS
non_builder_commands.rationale: This node-local cluster maintenance operation is deliberately excluded from automatic key routing.

non_builder_commands.name: UNSUBSCRIBE
non_builder_commands.rationale: Unsubscription and its confirmations are part of the stateful Pub/Sub session.

wire_contracts.description: RESP2 scalars, nulls and aggregates are decoded within configured size/depth limits.
Supported RESP3 scalar and fixed aggregate forms are decoded and normalized by typed response parsers.
Fixed attributes fail closed without consuming bytes; attachment to the following value remains planned in issue #705.
Streamed string/aggregate headers, chunks and terminators fail closed rather than becoming independent replies; bounded assembly remains planned in issue #705.
Whole-buffer and arbitrarily fragmented decoding have the same semantic outcome and error category for the tested corpus.
Frame wire size, aggregate cardinality and nesting depth are preflighted before recursive frame materialization, independently of fragmentation.

behaviors.description: Raw RESP2/RESP3 scalar, nil, empty, binary and numeric replies are compared with redis-rs. Separate typed live tests verify byte-preserving builders and public GET/MGET decoding, including ordered nil-versus-empty results, under forced RESP2 and RESP3.

Typed BLPOP returns a key/value pair when data is available and None after a Redis timeout on an exclusive connection. A separate multiplexed raw BLPOP test proves the configured response deadline returns CommandTimeout; the differential BLMOVE case is immediate because its source list is preloaded.

Raw hash, collection and Stream replies are compared with redis-rs using independent keys and controlled normalization. Separate typed live and parser tests verify HGETALL's public pair-vector shape, empty response and RESP3 map normalization.
Typed EVAL preserves binary declared keys and arguments and matches redis-rs for the tested nested reply.
Pipeline ordering and transaction commit/abort outcomes are compared with redis-rs without reusing mutating datasets.

SET outcome mode distinguishes applied and rejected NX/XX writes independently from unrequested, missing, empty and binary previous values. RESP2/RESP3 parser and live tests cover the complete supported outcome matrix; NX+GET and XX+GET branches are also compared with redis-rs. Expiry combinations remain outside this behavior row.
A typed XREADGROUP call reads new entries in a standalone consumer-group lifecycle, after which typed pending, acknowledgement, claim and autoclaim operations verify ownership transitions.
protocols: default Auto negotiation (RESP3 on the tested versions)

behaviors.description: Independent wire fixtures prove frame limits, aggregate preflight, nesting limits and fail-closed handling for fixed attributes and streamed forms.
Property and fuzz oracles compare whole-buffer decoding with arbitrary fragmentation plans and stable error categories.
Authentication, RESP negotiation and selected database state are exercised through connection setup and reconnect-aware paths.

One shared credential provider backs fresh standalone and Cluster sockets plus dedicated Pub/Sub and MONITOR construction. Provider URL setup preserves transport, selected database and RESP negotiation; lookup, forced-refresh, transport and session setup can share one deadline. A forced-refresh failure is redacted and stops setup before SELECT, HELLO or application traffic. Established ordinary clients can reauthenticate through owned tasks with explicitly documented owner-specific failure retirement, while Pub/Sub reconnects with confirmed binary subscriptions and MONITOR terminates/reopens rather than accepting unsafe generic in-band AUTH. Provider errors and refresh-task tracing omit third-party error text and retain authentication classification.
behaviors.server: Redis 7.4.3 and 8.0.6 per-PR matrix plus deterministic provider/unit fixtures
